PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST

To: San Francisco Public Works Custodian of Records

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.) and the San Francisco Sunshine Ordinance (S.F. Admin. Code ch. 67), I request copies of the records described below.

DEFINITIONS

"The Location" means:

(a) eastbound Page Street from Octavia Boulevard to Market Street, including all bike lanes, bikeways, and bicycle markings on that segment;

(b) the intersection of Market Street, Page Street, and Franklin Street, and the adjacent intersection of Market Street and 12th Street, including all traffic signals, bicycle signals, crosswalks, and markings within them;

(c) the route by which eastbound bicyclists travel from the Page Street bike lane into and along the eastbound Market Street bike lane, including any bike lane extension markings, green conflict markings, bike boxes, or turn boxes;

(d) eastbound Market Street from Gough Street through 12th Street, including the eastbound bike lane or bikeway (Class II or Class IV); and

(e) all raised medians, islands, and curbs within or adjacent to the routes described in (a) through (d). This includes the raised median in Market Street near the Page/Franklin and 12th Street intersections, the median's approach end ("nose"), and the flexible delineators, curb markings, object markers, pavement markings, and signs associated with it.

"Records" means writings in any form as defined in Gov. Code § 7920.545, including emails, text messages, messages on internal messaging platforms, drawings, CAD files, photographs, video, and data.

Time period. Unless otherwise stated, January 1, 2014 to the present.

RECORDS REQUESTED

1. Approvals. All records reflecting approval of the design, installation, or modification of any bike lane, bikeway, median, island, curb, or traffic control device at the Location. This includes San Francisco Public Works Board of Directors resolutions, calendar items, staff reports, and minutes; Engineering Public Hearing notices, agendas, and results; Transportation Advisory Staff Committee (TASC) records; and signed engineering approvals.

2. Alternative design criteria. All records concerning the use or adoption, for any bikeway at the Location, of minimum safety design criteria other than those established by Caltrans, under Streets and Highways Code § 891(b). This includes the resolution adopting the criteria, the qualified engineer's review and approval, and records identifying the national guidelines relied on (for example NACTO, AASHTO, FHWA, or Caltrans DIB 89).

3. Design documents. All plans, specifications, and design drawings at every design stage for the bikeways, medians, islands, curbs, and intersections at the Location, including final and issued-for-construction sets. This includes signing and striping plans; construction details for the median, curb, and island; as-built or record drawings; design exceptions or deviations; design memoranda and basis-of-design documents; calculations concerning lane width, clearances, taper or shift geometry, curb type and height, and delineation; and any standard plans referenced in them.

4. Bicycle transition from Page Street to Market Street. All plans, design memoranda, analyses, and communications concerning how eastbound bicyclists are directed from Page Street into and along Market Street. This includes:

    • channelization, lane-line, and conflict-marking plans for the Market/Page/Franklin intersection;
    • analyses of bicyclist travel paths, turning movements, or sight distance to the median(s) from the Page Street approach;
    • any evaluation of whether bicyclists entering Market Street from Page Street may conflict with the median(s).

5. Signal timing. Signal timing plans, phasing diagrams, and bicycle signal records for the Market/Page/Franklin and Market/12th Street intersections, including all changes and their dates.

6. Page Street bikeway projects. All approval, design, and evaluation records for bicycle facilities on eastbound Page Street between Octavia Boulevard and Market Street. This includes the Page Street Green Connection, Page Street Neighborway, Page Street Bikeway Improvements Pilot, and Octavia Boulevard Enhancement Project, to the extent they address that segment or its connection to Market Street, together with evaluation reports and the collision analyses underlying them.

7. Raised Bikeway Demonstration Project. All records of the Market Street Raised Bikeway Demonstration Project (Gough Street to 12th Street, installed approximately 2015), including:

    • the complete Findings Report dated December 7, 2016, with all figures and appendices;
    • video, staff observation notes, and data collected during the evaluation;
    • the reports of bicyclist collisions referenced in that report;
    • 311 reports, emails, and public comments received about the project;
    • records of any actions taken in response to the evaluation, including installing green paint or safe-hit posts, or modifying, retaining, or removing any curb design.

8. Subsequent projects and modifications. All records of any project or work order that altered the bikeways, medians, curbs, delineators, markings, signals, or signs at the Location after their initial installation, including work under the Better Market Street project and its quick-build phases and work coordinated with the Van Ness Improvement Project, with the dates and scope of each change.

9. Traffic control devices. Installation, inspection, maintenance, and replacement records for all traffic control devices at the Location, including flexible delineators or safe-hit posts, curb paint and curb markings, object markers, pavement markings and green bike lane paint, and warning and regulatory signs, together with any retroreflectivity inspections or testing.

10. Maintenance and inspection. All inspection reports, maintenance logs, work orders, and repair records for the medians, curbs, and bike lane pavement at the Location, including records of damage to any median or curb and of the placement of traffic cones or temporary devices on or near a median.

11. Complaints and notice. All complaints, 311 service requests, emails, letters, and other communications from the public or other agencies concerning the medians, curbs, bike lane configuration, delineators, visibility, signals, or bicyclist safety at the Location.

12. Collisions and safety analyses. All records of collisions or incidents at the Location involving bicyclists, including collisions with curbs, medians, or islands, and including incidents involving riders traveling from Page Street onto Market Street. This covers collision reports, summaries, and data compiled by the agency; safety studies, road safety audits, and Vision Zero or High Injury Network analyses addressing the Location; and internal evaluations of the safety performance of the bikeways or medians.

13. Internal communications. Emails, text messages, and internal messages among agency staff, or between the agency and SFMTA, San Francisco Public Works, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission, or Caltrans, concerning any of the following at the Location: the design, approval, construction, modification, or safety of the bikeways, medians, or intersections; bicyclist collisions with curbs or medians; or the visibility or delineation of any median.

Suggested search terms: "Market," "Page," or "Franklin," each combined with any of "12th," "raised bikeway," "median," "island," "curb," "safe-hit," "delineator," "bike lane," "transition," "crash," or "collision." Custodians include the Livable Streets and Streets Division staff responsible for the Location, and the author of the December 7, 2016 Findings Report.

14. Design standards in effect. The bikeway design guidelines, standards, or policies in effect when the bikeways, medians, and intersection configuration at the Location were designed, including any policies on delineating medians or curbs adjacent to bikeways.

15. Funding records. Grant applications, funding requests, and progress reports for projects that built or modified the bikeways, medians, or intersections at the Location, including Active Transportation Program, Prop K/Prop L, and federal funding records.

16. Asset and GIS data. GIS or asset-inventory records for the bikeways, medians, curbs, delineators, and signals at the Location, including installation dates and facility classification.

17. Photographs and video. Photographs, video, or imagery of the Location taken by or for the agency, including before-and-after project photos and construction photos.

FORMAT AND PRODUCTION

Please produce records electronically in native or searchable format where possible (Gov. Code § 7922.570), including CAD files or PDFs of plans and emails with attachments and metadata. Please produce records on a rolling basis as they become available. If any record or portion is withheld, please identify it and state the specific exemption relied on (Gov. Code § 7922.000; S.F. Admin. Code § 67.27), and produce all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions.

FEES

I request electronic copies to minimize costs. If fees are expected to exceed $20, please notify me before incurring them.

ASSISTANCE

If any part of this request is unclear or overly broad, please contact me to clarify it, as contemplated by Gov. Code § 7922.600.

Thank you for your assistance.

Marissa
